look_here_first: LOOK AT THE PAIRED GREEN BRACTS, NOT A RED LEAF SPOT. E. roemeriana is a small annual upright or basally reclining spurge (15–30 cm) with hairless, entire, obovate-to-oblanceolate leaves. Each flowering branch repeatedly forks; in the center find a tiny cyathium framed by TWO rounded green dichasial bracts that are JOINED for about HALF their length, creating a shallow cup. Tiny bright yellow gland structures have SHORT somewhat convergent horns; a smooth, roundish 3-lobed capsule develops nearby. Against E. commutata, the key is CONSISTENT substantial bract fusion rather than distinct or only barely joined pairs. E. longicruris instead has numerous tightly OVERLAPPING cup/leaf-like terminal bracts; E. austrotexana has far narrower leaves and distinct non-overlapping bracts. Mature E. roemeriana seeds have randomly scattered DEEP BROAD PITS and a prominent caruncle; two photographed mature seeds now show pits and caruncles; their absolute size is not photo-calibrated. This taxon has published HAYS COUNTY records in spring-fed Edwards Plateau limestone stream valleys, but the project's formal native-by-county certification remains on hold.

photo_note: Seven exact-species licensed source photos are installed, including five field/anatomy views and two Nathan Taylor mature seed micrographs. Seventeen arrows teach visible bracts, leaves, branch forks, cyathia, developing fruit, true deep seed pits and the pale caruncle. Pointers do not assert a precise half-fused bract seam or seed size without a millimeter reference. Remaining high-value shots are an isolated fused bract seam and rooted whole plant with scale.
taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia roemeriana Scheele, Euphorbia subgenus Esula section Tithymalus, separate from unrelated Amorpha roemeriana, Senegalia roemeriana and Phlox roemeriana. FNA identifies partly fused dichasial bracts as diagnostic against E. commutata and others. Peirson et al. (2014) document specimens from Bandera, Comal, Edwards, Hays, Kerr and Travis; this bibliographic county evidence is retained as a lead, NOT a replacement for the paused BONAP/NAPA county-nativity audit.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia subg. Esula sect. Tithymalus. The yellow structures are tiny cyathia (specialized pseudanthia), not ordinary petals, and nearby smooth 3-lobed structures are developing fruits.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual taprooted small spring herb, erect or sometimes reclining near base, 15–30 cm, glabrous; limestone stream valleys, rich calcareous soils, spring-fed creek canyons and floodplain terraces of the eastern Edwards Plateau.
morphology_keys.leaves: Main leafy stem: alternate leaves, blade oblanceolate to obovate about 5–20 × 5–10 mm, entire margins, cuneate/attenuate base, rounded tip, hairless faces, pinnate veins; petioles 2–5 mm.
morphology_keys.branching: Terminal pleiochasium normally forks into 3 branches, repeatedly subdividing 1–4 times into 2-part branches; larger upper bracts similar in shape to obovate main leaves.
morphology_keys.dichasial_bracts: Key: each CYATHIUM sits between paired broad green reniform-to-semicircular bracts, FUSED to about 1/2 their length; no teeth, rounded or obtuse tips. Existing single closeup shows a cup-like pair but exact fusion percentage remains noncalibrated and partly overlapped.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Tiny terminal cup/involucre 1.5–2 × 1–1.6 mm, glabrous, with FOUR elliptic-to-trapezoid nectar glands 0.4–0.6 × 0.7–1.2 mm and short 0.1–0.3 mm slightly convergent horns. The prominent yellow parts are gland structures, not conventional flower petals.
morphology_keys.capsules: Smooth, glabrous, subglobose slightly 3-lobed capsule about 2–2.5 × 2.4–3 mm. The image has developing green fruit, but cannot establish the measured diameter.
morphology_keys.seeds: Brown oblong-ovoid seeds 1.6–1.8 × 1.4–1.5 mm, with widely scattered deep and broad pits rather than regular ridges. A conic- or kidney-shaped caruncle approximately 0.3–0.4 × 0.4–0.6 mm. Need confirmed ripe loose seed photograph with millimeter scale.
best_field_traits: TWO green round/reniform dichasial bracts FUSED roughly HALF their length, forming cup below cyathium
Yellow horned gland structures at tiny cyathium (not true petals)
Glabrous obovate/oblanceolate small leaves with entire margins
Spring-flowering small 15–30cm annual of calcareous creekside habitat
Smooth 3-lobed capsule and brown mature seeds with DEEP SCATTERED PITS plus caruncle
Differentiate from E. commutata (separate or basally barely joined bracts) and E. longicruris (strongly overlapping terminal bracts)

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. commutata has paired dichasial bracts mostly separate or narrowly joined at the very base; E. roemeriana persistently has bracts connate about 1/2 length. E. longicruris makes very dense overlapping/IMBRICATE bract clusters and differs in seed morphology. E. austrotexana has much narrower linear to narrowly oblanceolate leaves with bracts distinct (not substantially fused). E. spathulata may have broad green bracts but bract pairs DISTINCT and often SERRULATE margins; glands without horns and capsule surface visibly WARTY; avoid relying on yellow alone.

field_matrix.roemeriana: RENIFORM to semicircular, united about HALF length
field_matrix.commutata: Separate or only barely basally united
field_matrix.longicruris: Often loosely joined at base but STRONGLY overlapping/imbricate at shoot tips

field_matrix.commutata: Similar shape and width, weak separator

field_matrix.roemeriana: Four glands with SHORT slightly converging horns
field_matrix.commutata: Check mature cyathia; tiny structures require a close photo
field_matrix.longicruris: More divergent and longer horns 0.5–0.8 mm
field_matrix.austrotexana: Crescent glands and diverging horns ~0.5–0.7 mm

field_matrix.roemeriana: Brown, scattered DEEP BROAD PITS, 1.6–1.8 mm
field_matrix.commutata: Seed differs by close detailed measurements; not inferred from current photos
field_matrix.longicruris: Gray/purple-gray smaller 1.3–1.6 mm with small strong pits
field_matrix.spathulata: Often smooth/reticulate/weakly ridged, not scattered deep pits

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: FIRST LOOK: do the green bracts actually join into one shallow cup?
steps: Find a spring-flowering plant on limestone or creek terrace and take whole habit + rooting/groundline shot.
Look under the yellow reproductive center: there are TWO broad green bracts. Follow the two margins down; do the bracts actually JOIN for a substantial distance (typically ~half)?
Contrast E. commutata: pairs mostly separate; contrast E. longicruris: terminal bracts strongly stacked/overlapping; contrast E. spathulata: separate/toothed bracts and warty capsule.
At 10×–20× inspect the yellow cyathium nectar glands with SHORT small horns, rather than confusing cyathium with petals.
Confirm a smooth, slightly lobed green capsule and photograph an actual ripe detached seed from two angles with a 1mm ruler; seek deep irregular pits + attached caruncle.

New seed panels: identify TRUE detached mature seeds with deep scattered dark pits; find the pale caruncle at the attachment end. These are not capsules or fruit surfaces. Do not infer absolute seed size from the photos because a scale is absent.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The paired green BR_ACT cup is photographed, but an isolated image proving its precise one-half fusion length is still missing; don't mark imaginary seams. Two real carunculate deep-pitted seeds are now photographed and arrowed, but do not measure 1.6–1.8mm without a ruler. Only FNA morphology supplies that size. County BONAP/NAPA badge still unreviewed.
